Thanks, everyone — it’s great to be here. I know that when people think about these big economic gatherings, they imagine speeches full of statistics. I’ll try to avoid that. But I do want to say something plainly: we’re all in this together. When one economy slows, others feel it. When trade works for only a few people, anger builds up. And we’ve seen where that leads. So the question for us isn’t whether to be open to the world; it’s how to make sure the benefits are shared widely. That means investing in education, in infrastructure, in the training that lets people move into new jobs. It means being honest about the people who’ve been left behind. And it means working across borders, even when it’s hard.
